edges.effect_quant: Pregnancies in women with PCOS show a consistently higher odds of preeclampsia in pooled evidence, and that excess risk persists even in newer higher-quality synthesis.
edges.population: pregnant women with polycystic ovary syndrome
edges.mechanism: PCOS brings together insulin resistance, hyperandrogenism, chronic low-grade inflammation, and higher cardiometabolic burden, all of which can worsen placental and vascular adaptation in pregnancy. That combination gives the preeclampsia association a more specific biologic footing than a generic obstetric-complications label alone.
edges.summary: The strongest contemporary synthesis reports higher odds of preeclampsia in pregnancies affected by PCOS, confirming the signal already seen in the earlier meta-analysis of obstetric complications. The older case-control study points the same way, so this is one of the more reproducible adverse-pregnancy associations linked to PCOS rather than a newly emerging concern.
edges.caveats: Some of the excess risk reflects higher baseline BMI and metabolic dysfunction in people with PCOS, even though newer analyses suggest the association does not disappear after adjustment. This edge should therefore be read as a meaningful risk flag that supports closer antenatal monitoring, not as a deterministic outcome for every pregnancy with PCOS.
